evidence: Python 3.14.5 py_compile passed for all implementation scripts and the test module.
Eight unittest cases ran without exceptions or failures.
The public API validates required observation fields, finite coordinate and bearing values, delta range, and tolerance range.
Bearings are normalized internally and no slope representation is used, including the 0/360 degree crossing test.
Each observation is implemented as the two closed cross-product half-plane constraints stated in model_assumptions.md.
Feasible boundary intersections are deduplicated, reduced to a CCW convex hull, and evaluated by rotating calipers.
The diameter-endpoint circle uses the endpoint midpoint and checks the maximum distance over hull vertices.
No arena clipping, reception radius, channel, movement, simulator, fitting, or probabilistic error model was added.
The validation seed is fixed at 2026 and the runtime records Python, platform, NumPy, and Matplotlib versions.
Two consecutive validation runs produced byte-identical q1_metrics.json content.
All seven deterministic validation rows passed and all 250 randomized convex-polygon comparisons matched the brute-force baseline exactly.
EMPTY, UNBOUNDED, and DEGENERATE states were each exercised and correctly reported.
The CSV table, metrics JSON, diagnostic PNG, and canonical run_summary.json exist and agree.
The tests cover angle wraparound, inclusive +/-1 degree endpoints, bounded and unbounded intersections, empty intersections, and zero-diameter degeneration.
An equilateral-triangle counterexample correctly returns diameter 1, circle radius 0.5, maximum vertex distance sqrt(3)/2, and no coverage.

warnings: No official numeric Q1 observation set was supplied; reported numeric localization diameters belong to constructed validation cases.
The bundled artifact Python lacked Matplotlib; execution used system Python 3.14.5 with NumPy 2.5.1 and Matplotlib 3.11.0.
